reader.decision: Implement the insert-first guard in charge_renewals with the unique index on (subscription_id, charged_on). Look up Payrail idempotency key support as a follow-on. Handle the duplicate dunning emails separately.
reader.decision_reason: The money-moving job must be safe on its own, and the scheduler dedupe fails after a restart because last_fired is in memory. The guard covers DST, restarts and manual reruns for the cost of one migration, while duplicate emails are an annoyance rather than a double charge.

reconstruction.problem: On 25 Oct Berlin clocks went back, so 02:30 local happened twice. The scheduler matches cron against local wall-clock time, and its 60-second gap check passed after 60 minutes. charge_renewals does not check whether a subscription was already charged, and renews_on only advances at 05:00 in settle, so the same 212 rows were selected and charged again.
reconstruction.what_breaks: 212 subscribers were charged twice (424 rows settled). send_dunning also sent the same 41 emails twice. Unrecorded manual refunds from Monday 26 Oct are a separate open item.
reconstruction.fix: In billing/renewals.py, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING into renewal_charges first and call psp.charge only if the insert took effect. Add a unique index on (subscription_id, charged_on) after dealing with the 212 existing duplicate pairs from 25 Oct. The alternative is scheduler-level dedupe by local date or running in UTC. It also fixes the emails but fails after a restart.
reconstruction.cost: One migration, including a pre-check for existing duplicates. If the process dies between insert and charge, that subscriber is skipped until the next run. The duplicate dunning emails remain. Payrail idempotency key support is unverified.

reader.closing_answer: Implement the insert-first guard in charge_renewals with the unique index. I would also fetch the Payrail docs for POST /v1/charges to check idempotency key support. The scheduler dedupe is not the primary fix because last_fired lives in memory.
